claim: Consider a simple bipartite ecological interaction network with \(m\ge3\) primary species, \(n\ge2\) secondary species, \(\max(m,n)\le E\le mn\) links, and no isolated vertices. Each primary species goes extinct independently with probability \(q\in(0,1)\). A secondary species persists precisely when at least two of its original primary partners remain. For secondary degrees \(1\le d_i\le m\), \(\sum_i d_i=E\), the expected surviving secondary count is \(F_q=\sum_i[1-q^{d_i}-d_i(1-q)q^{d_i-1}]\). Among all feasible graphs, if \(0<q<1/2\), the uniquely optimizing degree multiset is the balanced one with all degrees in \(\{\lfloor E/n\rfloor,\lceil E/n\rceil\}\); balance remains optimal at \(q=1/2\). If \((m-2)/(m-1)<q<1\), the uniquely optimizing degree multiset is the maximally concentrated one, obtained by allocating the \(E-n\) edges above the compulsory minimum degree one in blocks of \(m-1\); this concentrated multiset remains optimal at the upper boundary. In the intermediate interval \(1/2<q<(m-2)/(m-1)\), set \(R=\lceil q/(1-q)\rceil\). Every optimizer has at most one degree in \(\{2,\ldots,R\}\), and its degrees in \(\{R+1,\ldots,m\}\) differ by at most one. Hence exhaustive comparison of at most \(O(nm^2)\) such candidate multisets gives the exact global maximum. For example at \((m,n,E,q)=(4,3,7,3/5)\), the unique optimizer \((1,3,3)\) is neither balanced nor maximally concentrated. Nevertheless, averaging survival uniformly over all \(m+1\) stages of a random without-replacement primary-extinction ordering gives expected survival per secondary species \((d-1)/(d+1)\), so the balanced multiset uniquely maximizes trajectory-averaged robustness at every fixed \((m,n,E)\). All degree multisets used in the theorem are realized by graphs without isolated primary species. The two extreme probability thresholds are sharp for universal optimizer regimes.
integrity: The Bernoulli survival formula, single-inflection exact marginal, no-isolate cyclic realization, strict exchange inequalities, and uniform-random-cut identity prove the statements for every eligible finite graph. Exact-rational enumeration of small graph and degree cases tests nonstandard boundaries and equality cases but is not substituted for the general proof.
scientific_limitations: The model is a binary two-live-partner persistence threshold with independent and identically distributed primary-species extinction and no cascades. Degree optima are up to permutations; incidence matrices are not uniquely classified. The intermediate regime is reduced to a finite exact candidate family, not given as a closed analytic selector.
title: Degree-allocation phase transitions for two-partner ecological persistence
